The petitioners in M.V.C.No.19/2016 have preferred this appeal against the judgment and award dated 17.10.2019 passed on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - VII, Bilagi (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal') seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - VII, Bilagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.
3. The circumstances surrounding the case are that on April 10, 2015, at approximately 7:30 PM at Badagi Cross, an incident unfolded.
Annappa Ramappa Kolkar, the rider of the motorcycle with registration number KA-48/S-8773, had Suresh, son of Laxman Kolkar, as the pillion rider.
In a recklessly negligent manner, the rider operated the motorcycle, resulting in a collision with a divider.
Tragically, this collision led to Suresh, the pillion rider, falling and suffering severe injuries.

Despite medical treatment, he succumbed to these injuries on June 1, 2015, while undergoing NC:
2023:KHC-D:8906-DB treatment at Tatwadarshi Hospital in Hubli.

Consequently, the petitioners,
who are the legal representatives of the deceased Suresh, have filed a claim seeking compensation and have petitioned for the approval of this claim.
4. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2, who are the owner and insurer of the motorcycle in question respectively, presented themselves before the Tribunal and submitted their written statements.
The core content of respondent No.1's written statement is that they were the rightful owner of the motorcycle with registration number KA- 48/S-8773.
They maintain that, at the time of the accident, the motorcycle's rider held a valid driving license permitting them to operate the vehicle.
Moreover, they emphasize that the motorcycle was insured through respondent No.2.

In addition,
respondent No.1 contradicts all other claims and statements made in the petition, while simultaneously seeking the dismissal of the claims lodged against them.
The essence of respondent No.2's written statement, the insurer, is that the motorcyclist involved in the accident did not possess a valid and operational driving license at the time of the incident.
They additionally argue that the petitioners reported the incident with a delay of 15 days from its occurrence.

According to respondent No.2, the petitioners, in collaboration with respondent No.1,
have falsely implicated the motorcycle in question, with the motive of seeking compensation from respondent No.2, the insurer.
It is asserted that although the pillion rider sustained injuries leading to their unfortunate demise, the motorcyclist did not experience any injuries or damage, further raising doubts.

6. Moreover, respondent No.2 contends that the Bilagi Police failed to transmit the requisite documents within the stipulated 30-day period, as mandated by Section 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Respondent No.1, they argue, did not acknowledge the NC:
2023:KHC-D:8906-DB registration of the case under Crime No.90/2015.

Beyond these points,
respondent No.2 denies all other allegations made and seeks the dismissal of the claim petition.
On the basis of the above pleadings, four issues came to be framed by the Tribunal.

Smt. Manjula vs Sri. Balappa on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109433620/
3 7.

To substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 got examined as PW.1 and one more witness got examined as PW2 and got marked 15 documents as Exs.P1 to P15 in support of their contentions.
8. Respondents examined two witnesses as RWs.1 and 2 and got marked three documents as Exs.R1 to R3 in support of their defence.
9. After considering the arguments presented by both parties, the Tribunal reached its conclusions on the various issues raised.

The findings are as follows:
Issue No.1 and Issue No.2 were affirmed, Issue No.3 was partially affirmed.
The claim petition was partially accepted, resulting in an award of compensation totaling Rs.16,85,750/-.
This compensation comes with an interest rate of 9% per annum, calculated from the date of the initial petition until the full realization of the awarded amount.
In its judgment, the Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally accountable for paying this compensation to the petitioners.
11. Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioners are before this Court.
SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF APPELLANTS:
12. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellants has submitted his arguments that the Tribunal appreciated the evidence on record.
It is submitted that the deceased was hale & healthy and he was aged about 35 years at the time of the accident.
The Tribunal has considered the future prospects only at 30%, which has to be modified to 40%.

The deceased was doing cloth NC:
2023:KHC-D:8906-DB business and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has considered only Rs.6,000/- per month as notional income, same needs to be enhanced.

With regard to medical bills also, the Tribunal has not properly calculated the amount to be awarded on the said head and on other heads also, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on lower side.
On all these grounds, sought for enhancement of compensation.

SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF RESPONDENT NO.2/ INSURER:
13.
On the opposing side, the counsel representing respondent No.2, the insurer, has presented a counter- argument.
They contend that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal adheres to legal regulations and factual considerations.
Moreover, they assert that there exist no valid reasons to challenge or modify the judgment and award issued by the Tribunal.

Therefore, the counsel for respondent No.2 advocates for the dismissal of the appeal, NC: 2023:KHC-D:8906-DB maintaining that there are no justifiable grounds for contesting the existing decision made by the Tribunal.

Smt. Manjula vs Sri. Balappa on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109433620/
4 14.

In view of the above, the point that would arise for our consideration is:
 Whether the appellants/ petitioners have made out any grounds for modification of the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal?

15. Our answer to the above point is partly in the affirmative for the following:
REASONS 16.
With regard to the age of the deceased is concerned, Ex.P5- postmortem report indicates that the age of the deceased Suresh Kolakar was 35 years at the time of the death and the same is not disputed.
The Tribunal has applied the multiplier at '16' as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SARLA VERMA Vs. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER (2009 ACJ 1298).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has assessed - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8906-DB notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month which is contrary to the guidelines issues by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority (for short,
'KSLSA').
In view of the chart issued by the KSLSA, the Tribunal ought to have assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month as the accident in of the year 2015.

17. The Tribunal has assessed regarding the age of the deceased, Ex.P5 - the postmortem report clearly indicates that Suresh Kolakar's age was 35 years at the time of his death, and this fact remains undisputed.
The Tribunal, in accordance with the precedent set by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SARLA VERMA Vs. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER (2009 ACJ 1298), applied a multiplier of '16'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, a point of contention arises in relation to the assessment of the deceased's notional income.
The Tribunal evaluated the notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month, which contrasts with the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority (KSLSA).
According to the KSLSA's chart, considering the accident's occurrence in the year 2015, the Tribunal should have determined the notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month.

The future prospects of the deceased at the rate of 30% in instead of 40% as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND ORS. reported in AIR 2017 SUPREME COURT 5157.
18.

but the Tribunal has not awarded the compensation towards loss of consortium as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs.

sentences.text: Keeping in mind of the above said decisions, the award passed by the Tribunal has to be reassessed.
In - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8906-DB alignment with the Supreme Court's judgment in the case of PRANAY SETHI (Supra), it is pertinent to add 40% of the notional income to account for future prospects.
This adjustment results in a revised income figure of Rs.11,200/- (i.e., Rs.8,000/- + 40% [future prospects]).
Given the presence of five dependents, a deduction of 1/4th of the income is appropriate to account for personal expenses, equating to income at Rs.8,400/- per month.
Consequently, the claimants are entitled to a compensation amount of Rs.16,12,800/- (Rs.8,400/- X 12 X 16).

The Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.
15,000/- towards funeral expenses, but with regard to loss of consortium is concerned, in consonance with the judgment as laid down in the case of Pranay Shethi (supra), the Tribunal ought to have awarded Rs.40,000/- to each of the petitioners which comes to Rs.2,00,000/- ( Rs.40,000 X 5).

For the aforesaid reasons, is it just and proper to award the compensation to the petitioner/
claimants as under:
Sl. Heads Amount No. (In Rupees)
1. Towards loss of Dependency 16,12,800.00 2. Towards loss of Estate 15,000.00 3. Towards Funeral Expenses 15,000.00
4 . Towards loss of Consortium 2,00,000.00 5. Towards medical expenses 4,82,550.00
Total 23,25,350.00  Amount awarded by the Tribunal 16,85,750.00  Enhanced amount 6,39,600.00 21.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent/ insurer that the Tribunal has awarded the interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization, which is at higher side.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also keeping in mind the rate of interest on Fixed Deposit in a Nationalized Bank at the time of the accident, it is just and proper to reduce the interest to 6% per annum instead of 9% per annum awarded by the Tribunal.

ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 17.10.2019 passed in MVC.No.19/2016 on the file of the Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal - VII, Bilagi is modified.
